label: alg:q-beta-truncation
title: $\beta$-decay $\mathfrak{Q}_\beta = Q_{\mathrm{base}} \cdot \prod_k (1 + c_k\, u^k)$
html:
Algorithm. \beta-decay \mathfrak{Q}_\beta = Q_{\mathrm{base}} \cdot \prod_k (1 + c_k\, u^k)

Algorithm (\mathfrak{Q}_\beta truncation ladder). Evaluate \beta-decay Q-values via the convergent series \mathfrak{Q}_\beta = Q_{\mathrm{base}} \cdot \prod_{k = 2}^{N} (1 + c_k\, u^k) with u = b \cdot \hbar_q^2 \approx 0.00852, truncating at order N chosen by the target precision.

Input

  • Decay channel (parent isotope A \to daughter A').
  • Substrate q_0, electron mass m_e (CAL-1, CAL-2).
  • Pion-sector bar-even channel (CAL-3) for P_{\mathrm{avg}}^{\pi}.
  • Target precision \varepsilon \in \mathbb{R}_{> 0} → truncation order N \geq \lceil \log_{10}(1/\varepsilon) / 2.07 \rceil - 1.

Output

  • \mathfrak{Q}_\beta \in \mathbb{R} in MeV.

Algorithm

1. Compute Q_base from the substrate identity m_e · (m_n / m_e)
   modulo the binding-energy contribution.
2. Compute u = b · ℏ_q² where ℏ_q is the q-quantum constant.
3. For k = 2, …, N:
   c_2 = -1                  (structural: exact u^2 coefficient of the
                              explicit-factor product; not derived).
   c_k for k ≥ 3 are q_0-dependent NEAR-MATCHES; N is a truncation
     order, not an inclusion/exclusion criterion.
   Multiply Q_base by (1 + c_k · u^k).
4. Return \mathfrak{Q}_\beta.

Correctness conditions

prop:q-beta-categorical-precision-ladder establishes the precision ladder and the convergence rate.

The c_k coefficients are tiered:

  • c_2 = -1: structural — the exact u^2 coefficient of the explicit-factor product \prod_{k\ge2}(1 + c_k u^k), with no fit, no CODATA and no q_0. Not proved: the Lean re-reads the N{=}2 factor rather than deriving it. State which series — the normalised series' coefficient is \tilde c_2 = c_2 - 1/8 = -9/8.

  • c_k for k \geq 3: near-match with q_0-dependent swings (e.g. c_3 = -2 = J_{\mathrm{Hopf}}(q = 1) within \sim 3\% at the m_p-pin q_0).

  • The truncation order N is never reported as "fitted": it is a tier, not an inclusion/exclusion criterion. Individual c_k values are a different question, and some of them are fits.

    Corrected 2026-08-25 (PR #5765). This bullet read "c_k never reported as 'fitted'", which over-reached and inverted the discipline it implements. The AGENTS.md anti-flip-flop rule is "Report TIERED (proved / near-match / fitted), never binary wired/dropped" — fitted is one of the three tiers, so forbidding the label contradicts the rule. And the authoritative ck-dk-canonical-registry.md §3 applies it: c_4 is "EMPIRICAL — CODATA fit / artifact (mechanically confirmed 2026-07-11)", −0.97157, a CODATA residual that is "0 by construction". The registry's summary row is equally explicit: "Only c_2 = -1 is canonical … c_3 is a falsified near-match; c_4 is a CODATA fit; c_5+ are open."

    As written, this block instructed the reader never to apply the label the authoritative registry applies — an anti-fit-discipline inversion sitting inside the paper. What the rule actually forbids is collapsing the tiering into a binary wire/un-wire decision, which is what drove the four-session flip-flop (#1452 ↔ #1479).

    Also note the whole ladder is convention-C-frame and not yet re-derived under D (qou-cds1): QOU.QBeta.decayLadder_zC_threeRow_ne_zero (sorry-free) makes the C-frame ladder and the mass channel's three-row forcing mutually exclusive, so this is not a z-swap. Treat every c_k conclusion above as C-conditional until that lands.*

Complexity

O(N) — linear in truncation order.

Python API entry point

Canonical compute is the script computations/q_beta_predicted.py; run it directly to emit the per-channel witness. The CAL-3 pin is generated by build_cal_3_q_beta_witness.py.

Witness contract

Canonical witnesses: cal-3-q-beta.witness.json (CAL-3 pin) and q-beta-predicted.witness.json (per-channel predictions). Both report the truncation order N used and the tiered c_k classification.

Notes

The production neutron mass consumes a closed-form partial resummation of this ladder — the parameter-free Kashiwara b^2 truncation \mathfrak{Q}_\beta = Q_A \cos(\alpha - b\,\hbar_q^2/2)\,(1 - b^2 \hbar_q^4) (derived_masses.q_beta_kashiwara_n2_mev, wired into the neutron via canonical_mass.py and m_p_substrate_identity_50dps.py). Its outer factor (1 - b^2\hbar_q^4) = (1 - u^2) is exactly the c_2 = -1 term of the ladder above (with u = b\,\hbar_q^2); the \cos factor supplies the odd-b (N{=}1) correction.

Status: \mathfrak{Q}_\beta at \sim 160\times miss (1248 ppb, +1.25\,\mathrm{ppm} on \mathfrak{Q}_\beta) and m_n at \sim 181\times miss (+1.04\,\mathrm{ppb}) vs the (research-grade, sub-CAL-2-floor) 100× targets — both improved \sim 1690\times over the former flavor-split route. TIER: near-match; exact closure depends on the s_5–\mathrm{so}(3) fibre action (conj:s5-so3-fiber-action), which is unproved.
